title: November Examination
instructions: This paper consists of FOUR questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Show all working for calculations and include units.
Write in full sentences where explanations are required.

questions.prompt: The standard scale of an orthophoto map in South Africa is…
The name of a school is an example of…
Which resource is non-renewable?
The HDI combines life expectancy, education and…
Which type of weathering forms caves in limestone?
A gradient of 1 : 5 is steeper than a gradient of 1 : 50.
Physical weathering changes the chemical make-up of a rock.
Name the type of weathering in which water freezes in cracks and expands.
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Zone of set distance around a feature
Meeting needs without harming future generations
Downhill movement of material under gravity

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 50 000 map, a road between two towns is 11 cm long. Calculate its real length in km.
Trig station A is at 1 540 m and spot height B is at 1 360 m. On a 1 : 50 000 map they are 3,6 cm apart. Calculate the average gradient between A and B.
A rectangular plantation on a 1 : 50 000 map measures 3 cm by 2 cm. Calculate its real area.
A municipality wants to decide where to build a new clinic. Explain how it could use GIS layers to choose the best site.
questions.memo:
✓ Overlay layers such as population density, existing clinics and roads (1)
✓ Identify areas with many people but far from existing clinics (buffers) (1)
✓ Choose a site with good road access, not in a flood zone (1)

questions.prompt: A cyclist rides 9 km at 18 km/h. How many minutes does the trip take?
Which country (A or B) is more developed?
Use THREE indicators from the table to support your answer.
questions.memo:
✓ Higher life expectancy (82 vs 58) (1)
✓ Lower infant mortality (4 vs 55) (1)
✓ Higher literacy / GDP per capita (1)

questions.prompt: Why is GDP per capita alone not a good measure of development?
questions.memo:
✓ It is an average that hides inequality (1)
✓ It does not measure health, education or quality of life (1)

questions.prompt: South Africa is a water-scarce country. Describe TWO causes of water shortages and TWO ways of using water more sustainably.
questions.memo:
Causes (1 each): low/uneven rainfall; drought; pollution; alien plants; leaks; growing demand
Solutions (1 each): fix leaks; restrictions; rainwater harvesting; grey water; drip irrigation; remove alien plants

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between top-down and bottom-up development, and say why bottom-up projects are often more sustainable.
questions.memo:
✓ Top-down: planned by government or outside organisations (1)
✓ Bottom-up: planned and run by the community (1)
✓ Communities choose projects that meet their real needs (1)
✓ They take ownership, so projects continue after outside help ends (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how exfoliation takes place in a hot desert.
questions.memo:
✓ The rock surface heats and expands during the hot day (1)
✓ It cools and contracts at night (1)
✓ The outer layers weaken and peel off like onion skins (1)

questions.prompt: Name TWO landforms found in the lower course of a river.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): flood plain; oxbow lake; levee; delta; wide meanders

questions.prompt: Describe TWO causes and TWO effects of soil erosion in rural South Africa.
questions.memo:
Causes (1 each): overgrazing; deforestation; ploughing down slopes; heavy rain on bare soil
Effects (1 each): loss of fertile soil; lower crop yields; dongas; silting of dams; poverty/food insecurity

questions.prompt: Explain how tilted fence posts show that soil creep is happening.
questions.memo:
✓ Soil near the surface moves downslope slowly (1)
✓ It carries the tops of the posts with it, so they lean downhill (1)
